head: b7ee4555810dcb82b4a0714200c599ab076daac8
summary: Maintainers can now ask the agent to merge an approved commit when no required checks exist. The narrow exception preserves other merge gates, with approval enforced through agent instructions; usage frequency and time saved remain unknown.
reasons: The change closes the reported Ask-mode dead end and supports requirement R5: maintainers can ask the agent to merge an approved revision without adding artificial required checks.

The exception uses existing check discovery and merge safeguards. It adds one head-specific confirmation and result field, without dependencies, persistent configuration, or a parallel authorization system. Ruby verifies the head; the agent remains responsible for user approval and withholding confirmation under Auto.

The delivered scope matches the stated outcome: 12 files, 193 insertions, and 23 deletions in the final commit. Three review rounds and reported repairs do not demonstrate an approach problem; detailed repair diffs and original implementation commit counts are unavailable.
Instruction growth is reported as about 30 workflow words. The full instruction-growth report is absent, limiting assessment of total loaded instruction cost.
alternative: Keeping the GitHub merge click requires no implementation, but loses agent completion after explicit approval—the reported problem. Unconditionally accepting empty checks would lose the head-specific acknowledgment; no evidence supports that weaker safeguard.
next_action: Accept the change after the required human review of merge-guard behavior.
